newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's new CPMF rules won't be published Friday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's new CPMF rules won't be published Friday.

text.p: Brazilian Internal Revenue Service head Everardo Maciel said rules possibly exempting stocks from a new financial transactions tax will not be published on Friday.

Maciel said he did not know when details of the CPMF "check tax" would be revealed, saying he could only "guarantee" they would not be published in Friday's Official Journal. Earlier, a Finance Ministry official told Reuters the rules, expected to exempt stock market transactions from the 0.2 percent levy, would be ready soon. Neither he nor Maciel gave any further details.
Maciel was speaking to reporters after announcing record 1996 tax receipts of 95.096 billion reais.

Shares have been volatile amid speculation the government will find a way to exempt stock market transactions from the CPMF tax. The levy comes into force on January 25 and, as it stands, will be charged on all financial transactions.
The Central Bank in particular has expressed concern that the tax could lead to capital flight.
The tax is designed to raise some 400 million reais a month to fund the health services.
